1. Eur Rev Med Pharmacol Sci. 2023 Mar;27(6):2419-2427. doi: 
10.26355/eurrev_202303_31776.

Association of diabetes, fasting glucose, and the risk of glaucoma: a systematic 
review and meta-analysis.

AlDarrab A(1), Al Jarallah OJ, Al Balawi HB.

Author information:
(1)Department of Surgery, College of Medicine, Prince Sattam Bin Abdulaziz 
University, AlKharj, Saudi Arabia. a.aldarrab@hotmail.com.

OBJECTIVE: We designed this systematic review to summarize the diabetes-related 
glaucoma articles produced from 2011 to 2022. We further aimed to perform a 
meta-analysis to determine the vital association between these two parameters.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data sources like PubMed, MEDLINE, and EMBASE were used 
to find the relevant research. Reviews, case reports, and editorial letters were 
excluded. Articles inspection was conducted by the main author who extracted the 
study title and abstract in the first screening by using keywords to find the 
eligible articles. Heterogeneity was accessed by using the Cochrane Q test and 
I2 test.
RESULTS: 10 studies were reported with 2,702,136 cases of diabetes. Out of 
these, 64,998 incidents of glaucoma were observed. The pooled prevalence of 
diabetic retinopathy was 11.7% associated with glaucoma. A significant I2 value 
was achieved (100%) with Cochran's Q of 183.6.
CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, we found diabetes duration, elevated IOP, and 
fasting glucose levels are one of the leading risk factors for glaucoma. Fasting 
glucose levels and diabetes are also major contributors to elevated IOP levels.
